s.t: Vince Clarke was wary of Andy Bell repeating ‘respect’ in Erasure’s song, feeling the word was overused and invited comparisons with Aretha Franklin’s ‘Respect’. Bell stuck to his guns.
s.src: American Songwriter: How Erasure Found Soul in the Synths for Their Signature Song in 1988
s.q: Clarke was originally a little wary of Bell's use of the word "respect" throughout the song. He felt it had been overused, and it also invited comparisons to Aretha Franklin's "Respect" ... But Bell stuck to his guns, which turned out to be a wise move.

s.t: Peter ‘Sleazy’ Christopherson, co-founder of Throbbing Gristle and a Hipgnosis designer, directed Erasure’s video for it, taking the lyrics literally to extremes.
s.src: FACT: Sleazy Cinema: The music videos of Coil’s Peter Christopherson
s.q: the late Throbbing Gristle co-founder and Hipgnosis designer ... Likely one of the most-watched videos in the Sleazy catalogue, Erasure's 'A Little Respect' takes its literal lyrical interpretation to extremes

s.t: When a 2015 semi-final win sent Hull Kingston Rovers to their first Wembley Challenge Cup final in 29 years, fans sang Erasure’s song in full; Andy Bell heard via Twitter.
s.src: Sky Sports: Why do Hull KR players have song lyrics written on their shirts?
s.q: taking the Robins to their first Challenge Cup Wembley final for 29 years. At the final hooter, the fans belted out 'A Little Respect' in full ... Erasure's Andy Bell first learned of the song's connection to Hull KR fans when videos were shared with him on Twitter

s.t: When Erasure covered ABBA on their Abba-esque EP, the Australian ABBA tribute act Björn Again answered with an Erasure-ish EP of this and ‘Stop!’, reaching number 25 in the UK.
s.q: In June 1992, Erasure released their Abba-esque extended play (EP), which contains cover versions of four ABBA songs. In response, an Australian ABBA parody group called Björn Again covered two Erasure songs—"A Little Respect" and "Stop!"—and included them on their Erasure-ish EP ... number 25 on the UK Singles Chart

f.t: After Top of the Pops showed Andy Bell in a black rubber leotard and a rubberised ringmaster’s jacket, he says, their single jumped 40 places in the charts.
f.src: The Quietus: A Lot Of Respect: Erasure On The Strange World Of Erasure
f.q: I was wearing this black rubber leotard and a rubberised circus ringmaster's jacket ... once they saw that clip on TOTP the single jumped up 40 places in the charts, just because of that outfit.

f.t: When their computer crashed halfway through one of their first shows, at Heaven, Andy Bell did Alison Moyet impersonations and sang Beatles songs a cappella until the music returned.
f.src: The Quietus: A Lot Of Respect: Erasure On The Strange World Of Erasure
f.q: On the very first night it crashed halfway through the show, and I though 'oh my God what do I do now?' I just started doing Alison Moyet impersonations and singing Beatles songs acapella until the music came back on.

f.t: Vince Clarke found Andy Bell through a Melody Maker advert for ‘a versatile singer’: Bell was almost the last of about 40 people Clarke auditioned.
f.src: Electronics & Music Maker, August 1986: You And Me Both
f.q: Andrew and I met about a year ago after I put an advert in Melody Maker for a versatile singer. We did about 40 auditions altogether, and he was almost the last person to come along.

f.t: They opened a huge Italian festival with Andy Bell sitting on Vince Clarke’s lap; Bell enjoyed the whistles, only to learn afterwards that they were the crowd’s way of booing.
f.src: The Quietus: A Lot Of Respect: Erasure On The Strange World Of Erasure
f.q: We started the show with me sitting on Vince's lap at this huge festival. ... I didn't realise until after the show that was their version of booing.
